claims.claim: The marriage or civil partnership certificate is used for name changes.
claims.quote: You do not need a deed poll to take your spouse’s or civil partner’s surname. Send a copy of your marriage or civil partnership certificate to record-holders.
claims.note: The deed poll page says you can send a copy of the certificate to record-holders to take your spouse's or civil partner's surname.

claims.claim: The certificate is used for Marriage Allowance.
claims.note: The sources never mention Marriage Allowance.

claims.claim: The certificate is used for benefit updates.
claims.note: The sources do not say the certificate is used to update benefits.

claims.claim: A marriage or civil partnership ceremony must have been completed.
claims.quote: Your signed schedule is sent to your local register office where it’s added to the register. After that, you can get your marriage or civil partnership certificate.
claims.note: The page says you can get the certificate after the ceremony, once the signed schedule is added to the register.

claims.claim: The certificate is issued after a marriage or civil partnership ceremony.
claims.quote: Your signed schedule is sent to your local register office where it’s added to the register. After that, you can get your marriage or civil partnership certificate.
claims.note: The page says the certificate is available after the ceremony, once the schedule is registered.

claims.claim: The certificate acts as the gateway document for name changes.
claims.quote: You do not need a deed poll to take your spouse’s or civil partner’s surname. Send a copy of your marriage or civil partnership certificate to record-holders.
claims.note: The page says a copy of the certificate is enough to change your surname with record-holders.
